title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
abstract: A core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to balance three key requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, rapidly correcting sudden changes; stability, avoiding lasting model updates from transient disturbances; and persistence, retaining adapted dynamics during the observation-free open-loop rollout. Inspired by multi-timescale predictive coding in the human brain, we propose $\varepsilon$-WM, a world model that adapts to unknown dynamics through error-driven corrections across fast and slow timescales. $\varepsilon$-WM incorporates three novel features: 1) Multiple internal experts (MiE) emulate neural pathway reweighting, each combining a fixed base expert with fast--slow adaptation networks. 2) Fast--slow timescale adaptation captures distinct adaptation dynamics: fast states respond rapidly and decay, whereas slow states accumulate corrections and persist. 3) Predictive correction uses prediction errors to update fast and slow states and reweight experts without gradients. During open-loop rollout, each expert feeds back its own predictions, and $\varepsilon$-WM aggregates their outputs through adaptive weighting. Extensive experiments show $\varepsilon$-WM has a consistently lower multi-step mean error than all ten baselines on six datasets, verifying the effectiveness of each feature.

evidence.title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
evidence.abstract: A core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to balance three key requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, rapidly correcting sudden changes; stability, avoiding lasting model updates from transient disturbances; and persistence, retaining adapted dynamics during the observation-free open-loop rollout. Inspired by multi-timescale predictive coding in the human brain, we propose $\varepsilon$-WM, a world model that adapts to unknown dynamics through error-driven corrections across fast and slow timescales. $\varepsilon$-WM incorporates three novel features: 1) Multiple internal experts (MiE) emulate neural pathway reweighting, each combining a fixed base expert with fast--slow adaptation networks. 2) Fast--slow timescale adaptation captures distinct adaptation dynamics: fast states respond rapidly and decay, whereas slow states accumulate corrections and persist. 3) Predictive correction uses prediction errors to update fast and slow states and reweight experts without gradients. During open-loop rollout, each expert feeds back its own predictions, and $\varepsilon$-WM aggregates their outputs through adaptive weighting. Extensive experiments show $\varepsilon$-WM has a consistently lower multi-step mean error than all ten baselines on six datasets, verifying the effectiveness of each feature.

title: A Transferable Pretrained 3D Model for Impedance Inversion with Sparse-Well Prior Conditioning
abstract: Deep-learning-based seismic impedance inversion commonly requires retraining for each target survey, which may generalize poorly beyond the conditioning locations when well control is extremely sparse. We propose a transferable three-dimensional inversion framework that separates offline learning from target-survey deployment. A masked autoencoder first learns seismic structural representations from unlabeled multi-survey data, after which the frozen encoder is incorporated into an inversion network trained on synthetic geological models with sparse-well-derived low-frequency priors. During deployment, the complete inversion network remains fixed; the available conditioning well is used only to construct the low-frequency prior and align the global impedance range. Experiments on the Overthrust model show that the proposed method achieves the lowest full-volume NRMSE and reduces the P95 trace-wise NRMSE from 0.1310 to 0.1074 relative to the best target-trained baseline, indicating fewer localized large errors under different well locations. In a field survey with one conditioning well and three blind wells, it reduces the mean blind-well NRMSE by 20.95% relative to the target-trained U-Net while maintaining the highest correlation. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework transfers useful impedance information beyond the conditioning location with low deployment cost and without retraining the inversion network.

title: A Metalinguistic Axiomatic Theory of Intelligent Systems: Formal Structures of Cognition, Knowledge, and Theoretical Systems
abstract: English abstractThis work develops a metalinguistic axiomatic framework for cognition, knowledge, theories, intelligent systems, and AI. At the cognitive level, the framework distinguishes objectified items, registered meta-level interfaces, and residual metalanguage, retaining failure and unevaluability. Evaluation, object admission, name binding, and state writeback each have separate conditions. At the knowledge level, knowledge-base membership is distinct from verified or assertable status. Provenance, composite status, four-valued judgment, argumentation, tracing, and safe introduction serve distinct roles. At the theory level, theory objects comprise object and relation sets under co-rootedness and well-founded dependency conditions. Theory evaluation, transformation, and positioning have separate conditional interfaces. At the intelligent-system level, maintenance constrains optimization. Boundary, stable, and higher-order intelligence depend on stated criteria; AI generation and model scale alone do not establish these qualifications. Behavioral interfaces conditionally connect complete action, interaction goals and evaluations, and traceable joint descriptions. A six-step metatheoretical workflow organizes the deconstruction, reconnection, and reconstruction of existing theories. Task-relative textual and geometric representations organize theoretical expression and retrieval without replacing the underlying theory texts. The contribution combines theory-internal axiomatic or quasi-axiomatic reconstruction with cross-level interface organization. It makes domains, dependencies, admissibility, failures, and theoretical effects explicit. Empirical scales, engineering realizations, and system effectiveness require independent implementation and testing.中文摘要认知、知识、理论、智能系统与人工智能研究常使用相互分离的概念语言。产生结果与引入对象、保存信息与接受知识、改善输出与维持系统等不同任务,也因此容易混淆。本文建立一套元语言公理化框架,通过对象层与元层接口连接这些研究层次。框架区分已对象化项目、已登记元语言接口,以及当前对象语言不能吸收的元语言余项,并保留失败与不可评价。 在认知与知识方面,框架分别规定求值、对象引入、名称绑定与状态写回的资格。知识库成员不等于已验证或可断言知识。来源、复合知识标签、主显示、四值判断、论证、回溯和安全引入各有职责;它们不构成所有候选必经的流水线。 在理论层,理论由对象集及其中的关系对象集构成,对象集须满足共根与依赖良基条件。原始对象与基本原理由内部前驱读取,理论品质、变换和结构位置则通过各自的条件接口处理。 在系统层,维持约束优化,边界、稳定和高阶智能按明示判据区分。AI的生成与规模本身不证明这些资格成立。行为附录通过条件接口接入完整行为结构、互动目标与评估,以及可追溯的联合描述。行为分类不等同于趋人化或主体资格。 前四章的部分接口被组织为六步流程,并由四组异质方法示例说明。收束命题仅在各步资格与输入输出条件成立时连接环节;示例本身不独立证明这些条件。第8章规定任务相关的文本与几何表示,并区分假设与待定承接位。索引调用受答案覆盖、局部正确性和完整成本约束。 本文结合选定概念的理论内重建与跨层接口组织,明确各项内容的对象域或元层角色、资格、依赖、失败值与理论效力。工程实现、经验量尺和系统效果仍需独立实现与检验。 Full texts and supplementary materialThis record provides the full text in English and Chinese, together with separate English and bilingual Chinese-English theory-framework diagrams to support reading and cross-referencing of the main text. Companion website: yipenggu.com (planned to go online before manuscript submission). 全文与补充材料本记录提供本理论的中英文全文,以及英文版和中英版理论框架图补充材料,供读者辅助理解、定位和对照正文。配套网站域名为yipenggu.com,计划于提交论文前上线。
